key_insight: The paper defines "scalable logical qubits" as error-corrected qubits that remain reliable over long computations and can support fault-tolerant universal operations at application scale.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical benchmark for tracking progress toward utility-scale quantum computing by tying logical-qubit performance to reliability, scale, capability, and low-latency decoding.
method: Defines scalable logical qubits using four coupled dimensions: reliability, scale, capability, and performance.
Frames the target in terms of repeated quantum error correction, real-time decoding, and feedback.
Highlights trade-offs among these dimensions to make progress measurable and comparable.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and definitional rather than reporting new experimental results; it emphasizes a framework for evaluation instead of a specific dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: Achieving scalable logical qubits depends on low-latency real-time decoding and feedback, which may become a major systems bottleneck at large scale.
